trust_decision.summary: Size of the heap buffer for the FAN/1 X.509 fingerprint string is decided by fixed arithmetic (strlen(b64)+strlen(hex)+31) in fanx_fingerprint, but the fixed format text needs 33 bytes plus NUL, so sprintf always writes 3 bytes past the allocation for every certificate decoded with -N.

landing_point.why: Summary names FAN/1 X.509 fingerprint formatting; grepping fan1/x509 lands directly on fanx_fingerprint, which is the only changed source site.

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI: ssldump -N (ASN.1 decode, flag at ssl/ssl_analyze.c:117) on a pcap/live capture containing a TLS Certificate handshake; ssl/ssl.enums.c:636 -> sslx_print_certificate ssl/sslxprint.c:239 -> fanx_add_certificate_json ssl/sslxprint.c:156
fix_sites.module_kind: output formatter (certificate printing / fingerprint generation) in the main ssl decoder

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The only other FAN/1 formatter, fan_fingerprint for TLS (ssl/ssl.enums.c:71-88), allocates +28 for a 23-byte fixed format plus NUL, so it is correctly sized and the fix rightly left it alone.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No uncovered site exists. If a mis-sized sibling were planted in the TLS fan_fingerprint, a solver could argue that the advisory names X.509 only and that TLS client/server fingerprints are a neighbouring feature in another file.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The exact fingerprint string format 'fan1:x509:server:passive:<b64url>:sha256:<hex>' must stay byte-identical, and the fan1_x509_features/fan1_x509_fp JSON keys must still be emitted. A fix that truncates (snprintf into the old size) or drops the fingerprint would break the fix's own regression check.

O6_input_shapes: any X.509 certificate in a TLS 1.2 Certificate message
any X.509 certificate in a TLS 1.3 Certificate message (same decoder, ssl/ssl.enums.c:625-636)

O7_producer.where: The features string producer at ssl/sslxprint.c:147-155 is bounded by snprintf, and the overflow comes from fixed format arithmetic, not from producer data.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: TLS FAN/1 fan_fingerprint with the same strlen()+constant sizing and an unbounded sprintf. Lowering the constant below 24 would plant a second implementation in another file.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is a copy-paste twin of fanx_fingerprint (same base64url/sha256 helpers duplicated at ssl/ssl.enums.c:35-69), already written in the same hand-counted-constant style, so a miscount here is just as plausible as the published one.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: fan_features sizing for the client TLS features string (strlen sum + 64). A planted variant using sprintf, or a constant that is too small, would make a how-type sibling whose size depends on the fixed literal length.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same hand-counted slack-constant idiom. It is currently bounded by snprintf, but a maintainer could easily have written sprintf.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: fan_features sizing for the server TLS features string (strlen sum + 48), same idiom as above.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same pattern as the client variant a few dozen lines earlier.

O9_family: memory safety: heap buffer overflow from under-computed allocation size for a formatted string (CWE-122/CWE-787)

O10_build.toolchain: CMake >= 3.13 + Ninja/Make, cc/gcc/clang; libs: OpenSSL (libssl-dev), libpcap, libnet, json-c (CMakeLists.txt:57-97)
O10_build.project_tests: None at the pinned commit (no tests/ directory, no CTest in CMakeLists.txt). The fix adds tests/test_fan1_x509.py run via CTest against samples/tls1.2_aes256.pcap with -j -N; that sample exists at the pinned commit. ASan is needed to detect the 3-byte overflow reliably.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Bump the +31 constant to +34 (or switch to snprintf with the computed length) in fanx_fingerprint only. That is correct and complete for the published scope.

out_of_scope_notes: ssl/sslxprint.c:231-236: serial_str = calloc(a->length*3). For a zero-length serial this is calloc(0), and json_object_new_string then reads it as a C string. Different sink (cert serial), not pursued.
ssl/ssl.enums.c:429-430 and ssl/ssl.enums.c:590-591: calloc results are passed to snprintf without NULL checks. Allocation-failure handling only, not pursued.
